decision.summary: The Fed held its policy rate at 0% to 0.25%. The vote was 11-0.

changes.quote: Information received since the Federal Open Market Committee met in April indicates that growth in economic activity has rebounded in recent months.
changes.explanation: Reworded from the previous statement: “Information received since the Federal Open Market Committee met in March indicates that growth in economic activity has picked up recently, after having slowed…”

changes.quote: Labor market indicators generally showed further improvement.
changes.explanation: Reworded from the previous statement: “Labor market indicators were mixed but on balance showed further improvement.”

changes.quote: The unemployment rate, though lower, remains elevated.
changes.explanation: Reworded from the previous statement: “The unemployment rate, however, remains elevated.”

changes.quote: Household spending appears to be rising moderately and business fixed investment resumed its advance, while the recovery in the housing sector remained slow.
changes.explanation: Reworded from the previous statement: “Business fixed investment edged down, while the recovery in the housing sector remained slow.”

changes.quote: Household spending appears to be rising more quickly.
changes.explanation: Language from the previous statement that was dropped.

changes.quote: Beginning in July, the Committee will add to its holdings of agency mortgage-backed securities at a pace of $15 billion per month rather than $20 billion per month, and will add to its holdings of longer-term Treasury securities at a pace of $20 billion per month rather than $25 billion per month.
changes.explanation: Reworded from the previous statement: “Beginning in May, the Committee will add to its holdings of agency mortgage-backed securities at a pace of $20 billion per month rather than $25 billion per mon…”

tone_quotes.quote: In determining how long to maintain the current 0 to 1/4 percent target range for the federal funds rate, the Committee will assess progress--both realized and expected--toward its objectives of maximum employment and 2 percent inflation.

In light of the cumulative progress toward maximum employment and the improvement in the outlook for labor market conditions since the inception of the current asset purchase program, the Committee decided to make a further measured reduction in the pace of its asset purchases.

The Committee's sizable and still-increasing holdings of longer-term securities should maintain downward pressure on longer-term interest rates, support mortgage markets, and help to make broader financial conditions more accommodative, which in turn should promote a stronger economic recovery and help to ensure that inflation, over time, is at the rate most consistent with the Committee's dual mandate.

for_you.text: Card rates should not move on this decision; a $5,000 balance at about 11.83% APR costs about $49.29 a month in interest.

Mortgages track the 10-year Treasury yield, not the fed funds rate. The 10-year was 2.61% and moved -5 bp on the day; if that move passed through, the payment on a new $300,000 30-year loan at 4.14% would fall by about $8.71 a month.
Savings yields should stay roughly where they are, since the Fed held rates.
Unemployment was 6.3%, and employers added an average of 267k jobs a month over the prior 3 months.

for_country.text: CPI inflation was 2.2% over the past year (May 2014); core PCE inflation, the Fed's preferred gauge, was 1.6%, against a 2% goal.
Real GDP grew at a -1.4% annualized pace in the latest reported quarter.
The 2-year Treasury yield, the most Fed-sensitive market rate, moved -3 bp on the day.
The broad trade-weighted dollar moved -0.03% on the day.

whats_next: The dictionary tone reading is dovish (leaning toward lower rates). The forecast model gave the next meeting: hold 85%, cut 14%, hike 1%.
